content: Malate is the ionized form of malic acid, with the chemical structure O−OC-CH2-CH(OH)-COO−. It plays a significant role in various biochemical processes. In the C4 carbon fixation pathway, malate serves as a source of carbon dioxide (CO2) for the Calvin cycle. Within the citric acid cycle, (S)-malate is an intermediate that is generated by the addition of a hydroxyl (-OH) group to the si face of fumarate. Additionally, malate can be synthesized from pyruvate through anaplerotic reactions. The enzyme malate dehydrogenase facilitates the reversible conversion of malate into oxaloacetate, utilizing NAD as a cofactor. In plants, malate is also produced from starch within the guard cells of leaves. An accumulation of malate in these cells results in a decrease in water potential, which subsequently causes water to flow into the guard cells. This influx of water leads to the opening of the stomata. However, it is important to note that this process does not always guarantee the opening of stomata.
